    SAVE THE LAMPASAS, CARPENTER LAND & CATTLE CO., LARRY MARTIN,
      AND THE LINK N3 OPPOSITION LANDOWNERS RESPONSE TO ONCOR
   ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY, LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES
   CORPORATION’S OBJECTIONS TO, AND MOTIONS TO STRIKE INTERVENOR
               TESTIMONY REGARDING BARRY SMITHERMAN

         Save the Lampasas, Carpenter Land & Cattle Co., Larry Martin, and the Link N3

  Opposition Landowners (collectively, the Parties) file this Response to Oncor Electric Delivery

  Company LLC (Oncor) and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation’s (LCRA) (collectively,

  the Applicants) Objections to, and Motions to Strike, Intervenor Testimony (AIS Item No. 4726)

  regarding Barry Smitherman, and would respectfully show as follows.


                             I.      RESPONSES TO OBJECTIONS
         Applicants argue that certain exhibits of the direct testimony of Barry Smitherman should

  be stricken from the record on the basis of hearsay and non-expert opinion. Mr. Smitherman’s

  qualifications noted in his direct testimony as well as the CV attached to his testimony

  demonstrate his qualifications as an expert in this matter. Expert witnesses are permitted to rely

  on hearsay when it is reasonably relied on by experts in the field, even if the hearsay itself would
                                                                                                    Page 2 of 5


be inadmissible.1 Additionally, Mr. Smitherman has recently presented expert testimony in

Docket No. 59315 in which Oncor not only participated as an applicant, but provided rebuttal

testimony of a witness stating:

          I appreciate the insight and perspective that former Commissioner Mr.
          Smitherman provides in his direct testimony, as well as his recommendation for
          routing the transmission line to follow infrastructure corridors and property
          boundaries.2


          Oncor and LCRA object to three attachments. The first is Exhibit D to Mr. Smitherman’s

testimony, which is a press release regarding Post Oak Ridge State Park. This press release falls

under an exception to the hearsay rule because it is a public record issued by the Governor’s

Office setting out the governor’s office’s activities and Oncor/LCRA have failed to demonstrate

that it is not trustworthy.3 Additionally, Mr. Smitherman is an expert witness and entitled to rely

on this press release in forming the basis of his opinion.4 Furthermore, the press release is not

being used for the truth of the matters asserted in it.5 Its purpose is to show that the park exists

and has been opened, not the remarks made by the Governor, who was present at the park

opening, and the expression by the Governor regarding the importance of the park addition to the

state and community.

           The second objection is to Exhibit E to Mr. Smitherman’s testimony. Exhibit E is the

May 11, 2026 letter filed in this docket at Interchange Item 4620. This document is a public

record setting out the activities of the offices of the legislators.6. Also, Mr. Smitherman is an

expert who is entitled to rely on this letter in forming his opinion.7 Additionally, this letter is not

being offered for the truth of its contents, including whether the Permian Basin Reliability Plan

can be executed without the Bell County Big Hill transmission line, and that a third line is not

needed until 2030. Instead, it is offered to show the interest of several legislators who have

expressed concerns about the need for this project and a reflection of community values.8

           The third and last objection to Mr. Smitherman’s testimony is to two letters dated August

30, 2010, and September 28, 2010. The first letter is from LCRA to Mr. Smitherman. The second

letter from LCRA to the Commissioners of the Public Utility Commission of Texas. Both letters

are an opposing party’s statement (LCRA) and not hearsay.9 These letters were publicly filed by

LCRA in a prior PUC Docket 38354. Again, as an expert, Mr. Smitherman is entitled to rely on

these documents to form the basis of his opinion.10


                                         II.      PRAYER
           For the foregoing reasons, Save the Lampasas, Carpenter Land & Cattle Co., Larry

Martin, and the Link N3 Opposition Landowners respectfully request that the Administrative

Law Judges enter an Order: (i) overruling all Applicant objections to the testimony of Barry

Smitherman (AIS Item No. 4726); (ii) admitting the testimony of Barry Smitherman, with all

exhibits (AIS Item No. 4334), with such weight as the Administrative Law Judges deem

appropriate after consideration of the full record; and (iii) granting any and all further relief to
